recipes.purpose: In-capture backpressure: a saturated writer drops AFTER a bounded wait, and every drop is counted.
recipes.capture_config: VALID settings throughout: WriterWorkerCount 2, WriterQueueBytes 256 MiB, 1920x1080 native PNG, VideoFps 30. Saturation comes from a 250 ms per-job worker delay held for 600 ticks.
recipes.expected_arithmetic: At 1080p 8-bit the per-job reservation is 15.88 MiB (raw 7.91 + BGRA 7.91 + 64 KiB record), so a 256 MiB budget holds 16 charged jobs. Demand is 30 jobs/s; service with N=2 and 250 ms/job is 8 jobs/s. The 16 slots fill in roughly (16-2)/22 = 0.64 s, after which every arrival waits at most one capture-frame period (33.33 ms at 30 fps) and is then dropped and counted. Over 600 requested frames (20 s) the expected order of magnitude is ~150 committed and ~450 counted drops.
recipes.expected_gate: The GATE is on the invariants, not on the count: writer_drops > 0; EVERY drop counted (committed + dropped + cancelled == requested, no uncounted hole); NO enqueue wait exceeds the deadline; NO 10 s stall; capture_complete false. The count band is a reading, because it depends on the measured per-job encode time.

falsifier.defect_introduced: real in-capture service starvation under valid settings
falsifier.checker_that_must_trip: an uncounted drop, or a wait beyond the deadline, or a hole that reconciliation cannot classify
falsifier.corrects_A1_9: A1.9's saturation arm set WriterQueueBytes below one admissible job.
